title: Scammy it broken system
body:

I went ahead with the free 7 day trial to test it, at which point I was offered a promotional price of 24.99 for the first year. Like most professional apps, you’d think that this would then take the place of the 7 day trial and eliminate it as you’ve just purchased the year. 

Instead after the 7 days, I was billed the full 49.99.. So I paid twice for the same year. 24.99 and 49.99. 

Not sure if this is something they do hoping if enough people just don’t notice and rectify it they’ll pocket the money and it’s a handy little trick, or if they just don’t know how to run a business. 

If someone buys a year, you should not then bill them after a 7 day trial ultimately charging them TWICE for the same year of your service. 

Make it right.

And since almost every single Apple developer out there has now switched to this format, how many people do they think can actually afford to buy lots of apps that all have yearly subscriptions?

Since this stupid subscribe thing came on, I have not bought any app with this setup. I have gone out of my way to find a competitor who has a fixed price.

Now… I am pretty sure I bought Productive app a long time ago. I stopped using it a while ago, and when I opened it again to start re-using it, I saw this “you have to pay us monthly/yearly fees now to use our product.

title: Subbed for two years. In the end, not a 3rd
body:
This was an alright app for a bit of time but then it’s usefulness wore away. 

Two things really other me:
1 - after some time if you don’t swipe it stops reminding you. Maybe this is there to try to not pester you or something, and if so, it’s a terrible design choice. The whole reason I paid for this was to remind me of many little annoying things I have to do. I do not want to have to open an app as well as do those little annoying things. (After all if I wasn’t annoyed by them, I probably wouldn’t need the app in the first place) so this mechanic of it silently deciding to stop reminding me is terrible. 

But I tried to make it work. But then:

2 - the second, more, I guess, taste/choice based aspects that I don’t like are the little editorial comments on the reminders such as “just do it” “you can do it” “keep it up” etc. I wish I could turn that off. 

3rd, less important but still very annoying, is if you select a challenge and don’t click a thing within a 24hr window, the challenge sends you a “you lied” or “you didn’t follow through” message (those are approximate quotes: but it was something a little harsh sounding) and cuts off the challenge. Which if you were using, as I was, as a template for a cluster of good habits, just kills any enthusiasm and seems to be irreversible.

It’s like the app is needy. And if you don’t constantly tell it you’ve done the thing, it gets cranky. (Even if you do do the thing irl!) Then in its cranky state, throws a tantrum and just stops reminding you all together.  

That’s a deep structural flaw for me. Maybe others like it. I dunno. But given the other two issues I’ve had, it just made Productive less used and eventually I went back to the more reliable reminders app built into iOS. 

I’m one month one to a 12 month auto-renew, wish I had caught it in time, but oh well.

title: GET HABITICA INSTEAD
body:
TL;DR: The app itself is great, but the updates are never properly tested before release, so it’s always buggy and broken. Customer service won’t always believe you when you report a bug, instead giving you really insultingly simple tips that imply “it’s not broken, YOU’RE just not using it properly”.

This app often breaks and becomes very difficult to use after an update, so much so that I cringe when I see it updating. It’s almost as if no testing gets done before release. Use a different app if you’re an adult with ADHD or you plan to use it to manage your entire to-do list. (Habitica is great!) It’s just not going to be there to help you every day.

*Edit in response to the developer response:* Trust me, I have, way too often, and almost always because of a bug caused by an update. No other app in my phone has me emailing support as often as this one. So I’D appreciate if I could trust it to work.

*Update*
I’ve been trying for three weeks to get a bug from 2.0.0 fixed. The bug did not get fixed in the 2.1.0 update even though I was told it was being fixed. This bug is causing old, completed one time tasks to remain stuck in the Any time order list, and I can’t access them from another tab to delete them. In fact, some of these old tasks could be described as zombies, because tasks I completed in OCTOBER reappeared. Since the 2.0.0 update, the list has gotten longer and longer as I complete more tasks and they don’t disappear/can’t be deleted from the reordering list. Three weeks later, customer service is trying to tell me there’s nothing wrong with the app, I just need to delete the habits I don’t want anymore in the habits tab, completely ignoring that already explained that they DON’T show up in the habits tab, ONLY in the Any time order list, and therefore CANNOT be deleted. 🤦🏾‍♀️

*Update*
It took a month but my app is fixed and finally functional again. Yay? I give it three stars now because I can actually use it without much hassle now. Two stars off for unreliability and issues with customer service. Otherwise, this app is fantastic.
Edit: I take it back. The fix came with a new bug. 🤦🏾‍♀️ I swear they don’t test before release. I’m taking my third star back.

*Update*
Screw it, I’m switching to Habitica. I’m not wasting hours of my time wrestling with an app that doesn’t work. One star, only because I can’t give zero stars.

title: Should include specific days for habits.
body:
I stopped using this app because it didn’t accurately portray my week. 

If you skip a habit, it doesn’t break your streak but prevents you from getting a perfect day. So if you have a bunch of weekly tasks, your schedule will always be heavy in the beginning of the week. When you see your overview of the week, it’ll always show in the beginning that you didn’t have perfect days which looks discouraging.

For example, if you plan to go to the gym on Saturdays, Sundays and Tuesdays, then run on Wednesdays and Fridays, Productive will just remind you to do both in the beginning of your week. Since I don’t plan to do both on the same day, the first few days of my week will always show that it was incomplete. 

It would be great if you can choose specific days when scheduling tasks instead. For now, I’ve switched over to Habit List but am hoping Productive will eventually fix this issue.

title: Subscription
body:
I’m honestly disappointed that it’s not a one time purchase and it’s a monthly or yearly subscription. There is no justification for a subscription. It’s not an interactive context course and it’s not like it updates every month with better or more features. 

You want people to pay 18/year to get unlimited habits (other apps already have this feature), to get stats (people know if they did better or not or how long they did it without this feature). 

why would you even need a passcode lock for the app. It’s not like people are gonna specially go on your phone (that will already have a passcode) and be like oh man I need to know what they’re working on !!! 

Better reminders? Just set an alarm on your build in phone alarm? Other apps send you notifications to do it for free? And you want us to pay 18/year for a “light” theme? 

Completely ridiculous. 

I would’ve paid a one time fee as I need more habits. Even if it was $18 one time payment. But yearly? Makes no sense. I hope developers rethink this app business plan. Something must be wrong if they have to charge 17/year for “premium” features that do not add value when other apps offer it for free.

title: Near perfect mini-habit tracker
body:
This is the first app I've used that properly handles the psychology around mini-habits.

It allows you to retroactively complete an item (e.g. If you read after midnight you can still check it off, or if you forget to check something), and therefore the streaks are really useful and don't get broken by accident. 

The second power feature is being able to have a weekly task, or one on mon-wed-fri that is still tracked by streaks. 

This app has allowed me to remove my mini habits from Omni focus and keep that app dedicated to projects and one-off tasks.
